title: Power of Four
spaceBreakdown:
- no containers, arrays, or strings allocated
- no recursion (iterative constant-time expression)
- not counted: input n, returned bool
approach: A power of four must be positive, have exactly one bit set (i.e., be a power of two), and that bit must sit at an even position (0, 2, 4, …). The mask 0x55555555 has 1-bits at every even position, so AND-ing n with it tests whether the single set bit is at an even index. Combining `n > 0`, `(n & (n-1)) == 0`, and `(n & 0x55555555) != 0` gives an O(1) check with no loops or recursion.
hints: Write 1, 4, 16, 64 in binary, then write 2, 8, 32 in binary. Where does the single 1-bit sit in each group, and what differs between the two groups?
Use bit manipulation with a fixed mask. For n = 16 (binary 10000), the set bit is at position 4 (even), so AND-ing with a mask that has 1s only at even positions (0x55555555) keeps it nonzero.

**Zero** - n = 0 is not positive and not a power of four
`Input: n = 0` → `Expected: false`
⚠️ Bug: checking only `(n & (n - 1)) == 0` → returns true (0 & -1 == 0)

**Power of two but not four** - n = 2 has its single bit at an odd position
`Input: n = 2` → `Expected: false`
⚠️ Bug: checking only `n > 0 && (n & (n - 1)) == 0` → returns true

**One** - the smallest valid power of four (4^0)
`Input: n = 1` → `Expected: true`
⚠️ Bug: using `n > 1` as the positivity guard → returns false

**INT_MIN** - negative but passes the single-bit test
`Input: n = -2147483648` → `Expected: false`
⚠️ Bug: checking only `(n & (n - 1)) == 0` → returns true (0x80000000 & 0x7FFFFFFF == 0)

followUps.q: Generalize to checking whether n is a power of an arbitrary base k.
followUps.a: For non-power-of-two bases, bit tricks don't apply. Use logarithms: compute log(n) / log(k) and check if the result is within epsilon of an integer. This is O(1) time and O(1) space, but floating-point precision limits reliability for very large n.

followUps.q: What if n can be up to 10^18 (64-bit)?
followUps.a: Use the same three-part check with a 64-bit mask: `n > 0 && (n & (n-1)) == 0 && (n & 0x5555555555555555LL) != 0`. Still O(1) time and O(1) space.

followUps.q: Check if n is a power of three instead of four.
followUps.a: Bit manipulation won't work since 3 is not a power of two. Use the largest power of three in the int range: 3^19 = 1162261467. Return `n > 0 && 1162261467 % n == 0`. O(1) time, O(1) space.
